I farm in Quzhou County on the North China Plain, so at the start of the growing season I would keep to the cropping pattern I trust most: winter wheat followed by summer maize. At my age, I would not spread myself across too many crops, because wheat-maize rotation fits my land, my experience, the local weather, and the irrigation conditions I know how to manage. I would use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed because I want steady yield and stronger resistance, not risk from saving weak seed. I would keep fertilizer at moderate levels instead of pushing for the absolute highest yield, because I want reliable returns and manageable fieldwork. I would plough before wheat if the soil is tight and crop residue is heavy, then use rotary tillage for maize after wheat harvest because it is faster and lighter. I would irrigate wheat several times because that crop depends more on water at key stages, while maize would get fewer irrigations unless the summer rain fails. I would also keep pesticide use limited to what is needed, because I would rather control costs and avoid unnecessary spraying. My plan would be to run one full year of wheat in winter-spring and maize in summer-autumn on the same land so the field stays productive across the whole year.
